newsitem.title: USA: House budget chief sees Clinton plan deficit in 02.
newsitem.headline: House budget chief sees Clinton plan deficit in 02.

text.p: House Budget Committee chairman John Kasich said Monday he expects President Clinton's budget plan would yield about a $70 billion deficit in the year 2002.
Kasich, speaking to the American Association of Life Underwriters, said Republicans might consider asking the president to resubmit his budget with changes that bring it to balance in five years.
Congressional analysis of Clinton's tax cuts showed about a $13 billion tax hike in 2002 if the economy does not perform as favorably as the White House assumed.
Kasich, an Ohio Republican, said he doubted the Senate would approve a balanced budget amendment to the U.S. Constitution in its vote Tuesday.
But commenting on the plan Clinton sent to Congress last month, he added, "The president is nearly, almost $70 billion in the hole in 2002 in a vain attempt to balance the budget."
"I wouldn't be surprised if we ask him to send us another one that actually balances," he added.
Republicans have not drafted a counter-proposal this year and have said the president's budget would be the departure point for negotiations on spending and taxes.
